And then Genghis Khan sent his eldest son Jochi with fifty thousand [men] to the region of Khojand,
and his other two sons, Chagatai and Ogedei, he stationed against the city of Otrar,
while he himself went against the city of Bukhara.
And he commanded those whom he had left at Otrar to fight vigorously.
And when they began to press [it] hard,
that city held out before them for five months,
because Sultan Muhammad had left fifty thousand horsemen in it,
whose leader was Gayer Khan,
and another ten thousand whose leader was Qara Shah (or Qaracha? {OCR}) Khass Hajib, were likewise inside.
And when this Qaracha saw that they did not have the strength of the Tatars,
on one of the nights he took the majority of his own faction,
and went out through the Sufi gate to the Mongols.
They, however, kept him until morning,
and brought him before the two sons of the Khan.
And when they learned accurately from him all the affairs of the city and of its defenders, they said to him:
"Since you acted treacherously toward your master,
you will act treacherously toward us as well,
and we have no need of you."
And they commanded, and he and all those who were with him were killed.
And on that same day the Tatars took control of the city,
and they brought out all the common people, men and women, outside,
and plundered the possessions.
Gayer Khan, however, with twenty thousand chosen men of his own,
rebelled on the roofs of the high houses of the city and in the towers of the wall.
And they would go out on foot fifty by fifty against the Tatars, and kill and be killed,
until only two individuals remained with Gayer Khan on the roof of the palace.
And a multitude of Tatars gathered against them,
and toiled greatly until they killed those two,
and he remained alone.
And when his arrows were exhausted,
young handmaids were handing him bricks and tiles from the walls,
and with them he was fighting with the Tatars.
And because the command of the Khan was such
that they should not kill him in battle,
but capture him alive,
they exerted themselves greatly until they took him with caution.
